answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making every identity carry a slashable stake posted before it may act. A new agent must lock collateral and survive a slow probation where its weight counts for almost nothing, so one honest whisper from a peer can flag it and burn the deposit. Each identity also keeps a lantern of public signed history behind a basalt wall of cost that cannot be copied: to run a thousand puppets, an attacker locks a thousand deposits plus fees. Payback per puppet stays below the bond, so the attack loses money.
